body:
## About The Pull Request

- All maps are given preloaded drone spawners, rather than the few that had empty ones.
- Drone inbuilt tools are now considered Bulky.
- Heliostation distro piping has a few less unnecessary snags (Ventcrawling sanity)
- Deltastation Cargo had no connect distro. At all. It does now!
- Tramstation arrivals had no distro. At all. It also does now!
- Cyborg RPED's have received a increase in their storage capacity. 
- Removes a strange oxygen tank from deltastation fix:#6140
- Deltastation PTL now has connected Distro
- The Thesues teleporter AI sat is now functional fix:#6254


## Why It's Good For The Game

### Preloaded drone spawners
Just a matter of the wrong subtype being used during mapping. Drones are law'd to not care about anyone and thus noone cares about them. So they would never get mats placed into them spawning any drones.
### Bulky Drone inbuilt tools
Classic drones used to have a duffel bag storage. These like all backpacks have Bulky sizing, this means they could carry things such as construction bags or bluespace RPED's. This is a small return to that. They dont have the storage capacity of a duffel bag but they now can hold what a duffel bag can.
### Helio station distro piping
Heliostation had some redundant and dead end piping in its distro, this helps improve the vent crawl experience, while still keeping its maintenance centered distro in tact.
### Deltastation cargo
Delta station had no distro connections. Meaning every air lost to space would never be replaced. This. Fixes that.
### Cyborg RPED
Cyborg RPED's are underwhelming in their current state. Its side branch research that allows you to do something everyone else can at a basic upgrade. One of the most common complaints is that storage capacity sucks. Sharing the same amount as a basic RPED. 50. 50 total parts. We're bumping this to 200 parts for cyborg convivence. Which is less than the bluespace RPED's 400 parts.
## Changelog
:cl:
qol: Heliostation distro has been slightly adjusted to create less unnecessary snags. Actual distro is unaffected.
balance: Maintenace drone's inbuilt tools are now considered Bulky storage, the same as a normal bag. Normal -> Bulky
balance: Cyborg RPED's have now received additional storage capacity. 50 parts -> 200 Parts
fix: All stations merged have a proper preloaded Maintenace drone spawner
fix: DeltaStation Cargo now has a distro that is connected to the atmospherics and can properly restore air.
fix: Deltastation robotics airlock will no longer spawn with a oxygen tank
fix: Deltratstation PTL now has a connected distro
fix: Theseus AI sat now functional
fix: Tramstation arrivals is now connected to distro
/:cl:

author: lherskind
body:
# Operation Mouthwash

Named so because it is me washing out the taste of shit in my mouth after my registry code made it very easy to misuse which have put us into a hard spot.
# The Problem
The registry was supposed to be "per family", meaning that whenever there is a no inheritance (state) that goes from parent to child a new deployment would require a new registry. 

Because of this inheritance assumption the registry stores its own view of "versions" e.g., 1, 2, 3..., for the "history".

The fee-asset-portal for example follows what the registry says, AND pulls from its versioning to figure out what it should include in its messages. This puts us into a weird case when the registry is misused because the rollup might force the circuits to use `version = 1` but the portal will pull `version = 3` making the message non-consumable (unless our circuit code is buggy).

https://github.com/AztecProtocol/aztec-packages/blob/0951fb62e71149ee7de58c6ac13df5a8824d8369/l1-contracts/src/core/FeeJuicePortal.sol#L70

Furthermore, because we just used the same implementation we practically had that the version number were the same across all deployments (from the rollup contracts point of view). This have caused some confusion. 
## How did it become a problem?
The misuse of the registry was something that we did because for **EMPTY BLOCKS** it is not a problem that messages are not arriving or that fee assets are lost, as there are no need for any of them. This meant that for a "quick fix" for the zombie-chain, we could simple add another rollup from a different family to the registry and it would not cause issues.

However, as this was not clear we ended up not getting back to it, making it cause a mess now.
# Solution
Do deal with the problem. I think we need to replace the registry and fee asset portal implementations with ones that are less implied and can keep the same registry across families.

There is really two paths that I think we can take to get to that point.
1) The hard way
2) The easy way, but take a small L

The hard way is that we use the governance (which is only us) and do a big update where we use its ownership of different things to essentially replace EVERYTHING but the governance contract. 

The easy way, we abandon that deployment in its tracks, and we just run a fresh start with code that don't have the same issue. 

I don't think the hard way is alluring at all, it is more pain that I would really prefer, and I think it will be much simpler to deal with going the clean slate.

In the following sections, we will look at the changes suggested in code, and then the stages of gov and how they match.
# Changes and reasoning:
## Shared and individual deployments 
Deployments are to be more clearly be split out into a `shared` part that we only need to do once, and an `individual` part that is done for each rollup.

Shared deployment include:
- governance
- governance proposer
- fee asset
- fee asset handler
- staking asset
- staking asset handler
- registry
- reward distributor
- coin issuer

Individual rollup include:
- Rollup contract
- Fee Asset Portal
- Inbox
- Outbox
- Verifier

Where all of these contracts are tightly coupled. 

When an individual deployment is made, the rollup contract should be added to the registry.
### The rollup contract deploys its dependencies
To make it a bit simpler to deal with, I have altered the `RollupCore.sol` such that the rollup contract itself will deploy and link its `hard`-dependencies. Essentially removing the ability to pass in contracts that would be shared but should not be.

### Version becomes "kinda" chainid
Atm the version was a hardcoded number that was intended to go up as new deployments are made as code changes etc. However as there was often new deployments without L1 code changes the number would not change.

Also, the number was the same regardless of being on what network it was deployed to. To make the value more telling, and move it closer to a chainid usage for the future. I have altered it such that it is computed from the `block.chainid` of the L1, the string `aztec_rollup` and the rollup address. 

The ensures that devnet, testnet and such all will have different "version"s which should at least make that a bit clearer and easier to figure out where you are looking. 

Right now, it is based on a hash, and not really following the things that a normal chain id, does so I have not changed the name of it.

#### Registry and portal
The registry and portal are altered such that the registry is not longer influencing the portals, and now just keeps a list of rollups deployed without addings its own logic around their versions.

The registry is now taking care of deploying the `reward-distributor`, since I believe that at least makes it a big clearer that they are linked more strictly and just to avoid things being deployed nedlessly and cause confusion.

Lastly, we allow separation of the `owner` of the `registry` and the `governance` such that we can specify gov as the governance while the owner is just us, helping on the stages mentioned below.

### Inbox and Outbox
The inbox and outbox is currently made to go between versions (old thing) which means that users are providing a `version` as input. This is not needed when not following, so we can remove the input from user as there is only one acceptable value anyway. 

However, instead of doing this, we will simply limit it strictly. Reasoning being that we expect to use this interface again when we get to the point of moving state around, so keeping it should minimize pain to devs.


### Stages of Governance
Furthermore, the combination of the governance setup and how we are using it inflict more pain on us than needed. Namely, we have a gov setup with timelocks, but we are the only actor, and we are in full control, so might as well get rid of some of the extra steps for now. 

- Stage 0: We own of all the contracts. This allow us to just add a new rollup whenever we want. And is practically what we have now, just with less pain around how we are running it.
- Stage 1: We own all the contracts, but will look at signals that sequencers are sending. This is practically 0, just with them signalling.
- Stage 2: We pass ownership of most contracts to the governance, but still keep the staking asset such that we can mint and force things.
- Stage 3: We hand tokens out to others to vote, and practically don't have to be part of it anymore.

# How does a new deployment look

This depends on what exact stage we are at, but I'm inclined to alter the setup so we don't have scripts for going through and faking governance as much as we are now since we might as well just skip it and deal with it MUCH simpler directly in the deployment.

This means that for the early stages, e.g., 0 and 1, we could just directly update. And we are just testing the signalling to test.
# Conclusion
The mix of staging the governance and altering the contracts, means that it is possible for us to give just a single registry address that is stable across all the versions. But also gives us the power to deal with upgrades more simply short term because the deployment can simply add it to the registry skipping a bunch of these extra steps.

body:
This pull request introduces several significant changes to the handling of function literals, closures, and symbol resolution in the codebase. The changes include modifications to the AST structure, the addition of new opcodes, updates to the compiler and symbol table, and extensive updates to the test cases to support and validate the new functionality.

### AST and Function Literals:
* Added a `Name` field to the `FunctionLiteral` struct to store the function's name. (`ast/ast.go` [ast/ast.goR228](diffhunk://#diff-9dcefbf65d58a909b6cc7332b7985d070382bf920a4b13c7acea4ee91ecdf5acR228))
* Updated the `String` method of `FunctionLiteral` to include the function's name if it is not empty. (`ast/ast.go` [ast/ast.goR243-R245](diffhunk://#diff-9dcefbf65d58a909b6cc7332b7985d070382bf920a4b13c7acea4ee91ecdf5acR243-R245))

### New Opcodes and Definitions:
* Introduced new opcodes: `OpClosure`, `OpGetFree`, and `OpCurrentClosure`. (`code/code.go` [code/code.goR46-R48](diffhunk://#diff-2ad350013d16e8e5c021ee6f046700bb0b8249a3baa1fe88c79aac3c06c214bbR46-R48))
* Updated the `definitions` map to include the new opcodes with their respective operand counts. (`code/code.go` [code/code.goR79-R81](diffhunk://#diff-2ad350013d16e8e5c021ee6f046700bb0b8249a3baa1fe88c79aac3c06c214bbR79-R81))
* Modified the `fmtInstruction` method to handle instructions with two operands. (`code/code.go` [code/code.goR176-R177](diffhunk://#diff-2ad350013d16e8e5c021ee6f046700bb0b8249a3baa1fe88c79aac3c06c214bbR176-R177))

### Compiler Enhancements:
* Adjusted the `Compile` method to define function names and handle free symbols when compiling function literals. (`compiler/compiler.go` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-d3cde2dec4b7c2263747b17d43f704418e6657b49583254628bcad1d1052471bR238-R240) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d3cde2dec4b7c2263747b17d43f704418e6657b49583254628bcad1d1052471bR256-R269)
* Updated the `loadSymbol` method to emit the correct opcodes for free and function scope symbols. (`compiler/compiler.go` [compiler/compiler.goR405-R408](diffhunk://#diff-d3cde2dec4b7c2263747b17d43f704418e6657b49583254628bcad1d1052471bR405-R408))

### Symbol Table Updates:
* Added `FreeScope` and `FunctionScope` to the `SymbolScope` type. (`compiler/symbol_table.go` [compiler/symbol_table.goR9-R10](diffhunk://#diff-cf3d9e23db2aed625c3ebd5e3a3c14ace3c3c5e055c2e555f5b8474dcf2b1b45R9-R10))
* Introduced the `FreeSymbols` slice in the `SymbolTable` struct to track free symbols. (`compiler/symbol_table.go` [compiler/symbol_table.goR23-R29](diffhunk://#diff-cf3d9e23db2aed625c3ebd5e3a3c14ace3c3c5e055c2e555f5b8474dcf2b1b45R23-R29))
* Implemented `DefineFree` and `DefineFunctionName` methods to handle free symbols and function names. (`compiler/symbol_table.go` [compiler/symbol_table.goR71-R84](diffhunk://#diff-cf3d9e23db2aed625c3ebd5e3a3c14ace3c3c5e055c2e555f5b8474dcf2b1b45R71-R84))

### Test Cases:
* Added extensive test cases to validate the new functionality, including tests for closures and recursive functions. (`compiler/compiler_test.go` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-cc1616f55ca6edd2c0685642afa94d589da91d1bf06e7b787695782b16dd5145R882-R1075) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-cc1616f55ca6edd2c0685642afa94d589da91d1bf06e7b787695782b16dd5145L826-R843)

These changes collectively enhance the language's support for closures and improve the handling of function literals and symbol resolution.

author: lassoan
body:
Note that this PR is marked as Draft  because it currently contains commits from other PRs that are being reviewed. They will be removed from this PR when they are merged and this PR is rebased. Only review the last commit (`ENH: Refactor observations in MRML nodes`).

---

As described in https://www.slicer.org/wiki/Slicer3:EventBroker documentation:
VTK observations can be added at 3 different levels: plain VTK, EventBroker, ObserverManager.
ObserverManager is the highest-level, safest and most convenient API and should be used in all MRML nodes.

This commit updates MRML nodes to meet this recommendation. Specifically:

- Replace plain VTK API:
  - Replace `object->AddObserver()` by `vtkObserveMRMLObjectMacro(object)`
  - Replace `object->RemoveObserver()` by `vtkUnObserveMRMLObjectMacro(object)`
  - Replace `if (!node->HasObserver(...)) { node->AddObserver(...) }` by `vtkObserveMRMLObjectEventNoWarningMacro`
- Replace EventBroker API:
  - Replace `vtkEventBroker::GetInstance()->AddObservation(...)` by `vtkObserveMRMLObjectMacro(this->Camera)`
  - Replace `vtkEventBroker::GetInstance()->RemoveObservations(...)` by `vtkUnObserveMRMLObjectMacro(this->Camera)`
  - Replace `if (!broker->GetObservationExist(...)) { broker->AddObservation(...) }` by `vtkObserveMRMLObjectEventNoWarningMacro`
  - Replace EventBroker-based SetAndObserve implementations by `vtkSetAndObserveMRMLObjectMacro`
- Related cleanup:
  - Add missing `vtkUnObserveMRMLObjectMacro(...)` before observing a new object
  - Remove unnecessary `this->RemoveObservers(...)` in destructors (`ObserverManager` takes care of removing observers)
  - Remove unnecessary `vtkEventBroker.h` and `vtkCallbackCommand.h` includes.
- Added https://www.slicer.org/wiki/Slicer3:EventBroker to documentation

body:
I wanted to be able to derive `Encode` and `Decode` for various message types in RFC 4253 and related RFCs. As the current implementation has some limitations (and I wanted to get some more macro-writing practice), I've gone ahead and extended `ssh-derive` quite a bit. The result is a rather substantial refactor, but it now supports all types of structs as well as enums. I realize this might be a bit much to review, but seeing as `ssh-derive` is `0.0.1-alpha` I figured it might be alright.

This PR is really in two parts (let me know if it is better merged as two separate things):

- `ssh-derive`: 
    - Allow deriving `Encode`/`Decode` on all kinds of structs and enums.
    - Introduce derive attributes to control the generated impls.
        - `#[ssh(length_prefixed)]` to use length prefixing when encoding/decoding. Can be applies to the struct/enum itself, or to individual fields.
        - `#[repr(u8)]` and friends: Enum discriminants will encode/decode with the type specified by the `repr` attribute.
- `ssh-encoding`:
    - Add a `derive` feature that re-exports the derive macros from `ssh-derive`.
    - Add a new error variant to `ssh_encoding::Error` to handle unexpected discriminant values when decoding.
    - Add tests and documentation for the `derive` feature.

body:
This patch adds an explicit type conversion to avoid the ambiguity:
```
assert!(
    keys.len()
        <= usize::try_from(u32::MAX)
            .expect("we don't support 16-bit systems")
);

```
When you self compile Vector with `time` or `domain` crate, you will meet this error:
```
error[E0283]: type annotations needed
   --> /home/suika/.cargo/git/checkouts/vector-7010c25277c07669/063cabb/lib/vector-core/src/metrics/ddsketch.rs:460:22
    |
459 |                 <= u32::MAX
    |                 -- type must be known at this point
460 |                     .try_into()
    |                      ^^^^^^^^
    |
    = note: multiple `impl`s satisfying `usize: PartialOrd<_>` found in the following crates: `core`, `deranged`:
            - impl PartialOrd for usize;
            - impl<MIN, MAX> PartialOrd<deranged::RangedUsize<MIN, MAX>> for usize
              where the constant `MIN` has type `usize`, the constant `MAX` has type `usize`;
help: try using a fully qualified path to specify the expected types
    |
459 |                 <= <u32 as TryInto<T>>::try_into(u32::MAX)
    |                    ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++       
```
We can use  turbofish syntax (.try_into::<usize>()) to explicit specify which type we need.

- **Action Tracking**: Added the ability to track actions taken on reports, such as issuing warnings, banning users, or dismissing the report.

This layout is a niche within a niche within a niche: [AdNW](http://www.adnw.de/) is a layout optimized for a German/English split, similar what Dvorak did for English and Neo did for German. AdNW BuT is a variant of AdNW created for the [Truly Ergonomic keyboard](https://trulyergonomic.com/) and similar ortholinear keyboards. AdNW BuT-XCV is a mirrored variant of that.

I'm learning to type this niche layout on a ZSA Moonlander and a ZSA Voyager at the moment, and I'd love to use keybr for that, but having a wrong layout on screen is confusing.

Is this too niche for upstream inclusion? There's probably only a handful of people that will ever use this.
